脅.meaning: Under the <part>moon</part>, three <part>strongmen</part> catch a raccoon in their kitchen and flex at it, growling, 'Drop the cupcake.' The raccoon flexes back, tiny arms trembling, and keeps chewing. It's hard to <kanji>threaten</kanji> someone that hungry.
脅.on: It waddles off with a souvenir mug that says '<sound>Kyo</sound>to', crooning the name with a long, stretched start.
脅.kun: An <sound>o</sound>tter and a <sound>bee</sound>tle cheer the raccoon on from the window: '<sound>Yah</sound>!'

描.meaning: A sailor, bored on a flat calm sea, uses the sharp tip of his <part>anchor</part> to scratch a <part>seedling</part> onto the deck: two tiny leaves, a curly root. The captain loves it and frames the plank. Not bad for a quick <kanji>sketch</kanji>.
描.on: A <sound>bee</sound> lands on the plank and flicks a tiny <sound>yo</sound>-yo across the drawing, long and slow.
描.kun: For his next drawing he scratches an <sound>e</sound>gg beside a bulb of <sound>ga</sound>rlic.

孤.meaning: In a pumpkin patch, one <part>melon</part> grows all by itself, with no vine-mates and no family. A <part>child</part> spots it, draws it a smile and wheels it home in a wagon to sit by the fire. Every lonely <kanji>orphan</kanji> deserves a home.
孤.on: Her pet <sound>ko</sound>ala hugs the melon all night so it never feels alone.

殿.meaning: A <part>maiden</part> and her little brother build a snowman <part>together</part>, give him a <part>flag</part> for a walking stick and argue all afternoon about his name. They run out of paint after the first two letters and a dot, so that's all his hat says: <kanji>Mr.</kanji>
殿.on: Their dad, a <sound>den</sound>tist, gives the snowman a full set of pebble teeth.
殿.kun: The snowman gets a <sound>to</sound>p hat, <sound>no</sound>t a cap, to go with his new name.

雲.meaning: A girl's <part>kite</part> climbs so high it tangles in something fluffy and grey and drags it home like a balloon. She ties it to her bedpost, where it drips <part>rain</part> on her goldfish all night. Her new pet is a <kanji>cloud</kanji>.
雲.on: She feeds it rainwater from a sp<sound>oon</sound> every morning.
雲.kun: Her mum, the <sound>coo</sound>k, follows it round the house with a <sound>mo</sound>p.

屯.meaning: A drill sergeant draws a <part>slash</part> in the mud and orders the troops to sleep behind it, then finds a <part>sprout</part> poking up in the middle of the camp. He waters it every dawn, salutes it, and gives it its own bunk in the <kanji>barracks</kanji>.
屯.on: In the mess hall, he serves its water with a giant pair of <sound>ton</sound>gs.
屯.kun: On Fridays the troops eat a <sound>ta</sound>co, ride a <sound>moo</sound>se and launch a toy <sound>ro</sound>cket.

純.meaning: At a market, a seller swears his silk is real. To prove it, he ties a single <part>thread</part> from a <part>hitching post</part> to a bull and lets it pull. The bull strains, the post creaks, the thread holds. The crowd buys every roll: it's <kanji>genuine</kanji>.
純.on: The bull gets a whole <sound>jun</sound>iper bush to munch as thanks.

遇.meaning: A <part>gumball machine</part> tips over at the top of a <part>ramp</part>, and every gumball rolls down, red, blue, green, clacking into one friendly heap at the bottom. Strangers kneel to pick them up and end up chatting. What a way to <kanji>meet</kanji>.
遇.on: Two of them get stuck together in a blob of <sound>goo</sound> and refuse to let go.
遇.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, it's you!' says one stranger to another, waving a sticky hand.

署.meaning: <part>Someone</part> at the bank forgets his pen, so he dips his fishing <part>net</part> in the ink pot and swipes it across the cheque, leaving a criss-cross smudge. The clerk squints, shrugs and stamps it. Nobody will ever forge that <kanji>signature</kanji>.
署.on: On the way home he buys a spare net at the bait <sound>sho</sound>p, ready for the next cheque.

叫.meaning: A choir teacher taps a <part>tuning fork</part> on the piano, and instead of a soft hum, a tiny <part>mouth</part> on its handle bellows 'TUESDAY!' Everyone jumps out of their seats. That fork can't hum at all; it can only <kanji>shout</kanji>.
叫.on: Next it yells '<sound>Kyo</sound>to!', holding the first part until the windows rattle.
叫.kun: A lady in a <sound>sa</sound>ri drops her <sound>ke</sound>ttle in fright.

釈.meaning: A bear teacher lays her <part>paw</part> on the chalkboard beside a tape <part>measure</part> to show how big a fish she caught, then talks for an hour about why it was really twice that size. The cubs nod, lost. Her lesson is one long <kanji>explanation</kanji>.
釈.on: The fish, she insists, was nearly the size of a <sound>shar</sound>k.
釈.kun: She ends by drawing it on <sound>to</sound>p of a stove, with a <sound>coo</sound>k frying it.

盲.meaning: A stonemason carves a grand <part>tombstone</part> for an old pirate and adds one carved <part>eye</part> with a patch over it, as the pirate wished. Crows land on it and peer into the stone eye, puzzled: it sees nothing. It is <kanji>blind</kanji>.
盲.on: Every Sunday the groundskeeper's <sound>mo</sound>wer hums slowly around it.

凍.meaning: A man walks <part>east</part> to watch the sunrise and stands there admiring it so long that <part>ice</part> creeps up his boots, his beard and his nose. By noon he's a smiling statue with pigeons on his hat. He's completely <kanji>frozen</kanji>.
凍.on: Only his big <sound>toe</sound> still wiggles inside his boot.
凍.kun: A kid sticks an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne in his hand, and it never melts.

距.meaning: A <part>giant</part> cowboy wants his horse to go faster, so he straps a whole windmill wheel to the heel of each <part>foot</part>. It spins and jingles as he walks, ploughing deep grooves across the prairie. That's one big <kanji>spur</kanji>.
距.on: He stops at a <sound>kio</sound>sk for coffee, and the jingling wakes the whole street.
距.kun: A <sound>he</sound>n and a <sound>du</sound>ck keep well back from his spinning heels.

蓄.meaning: A sheep who doesn't trust winter hides mouthfuls of <part>grass</part> under the barn floor every day while the other <part>livestock</part> nap. By December she's perched on a hay mountain up to the rafters. She has managed to <kanji>amass</kanji> a fortune in snacks.
蓄.on: She tops the pile with one <sound>chic</sound>kpea, like a cherry on a cake.
蓄.kun: She hides a <sound>ta</sound>co, a <sound>coo</sound>kie and a tube of <sound>wa</sound>sabi in there too.

軟.meaning: A <part>car</part> lets out an enormous <part>yawn</part> in the car park, and its whole body goes floppy: the roof sags, the tyres squish like marshmallows and the doors droop like ears. Kids bounce on it like a bed. It's gone completely <kanji>soft</kanji>.
軟.on: The driver plugs a hole in one tyre with a folded <sound>naan</sound>, and somehow it holds.
軟.kun: '<sound>Yah</sound>!' whoops a kid as he bounces, and the car groans '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

竜.meaning: A lizard eats a whole chilli pepper on a dare. Its tail swishes, wings burst from its shoulders and a puff of fire singes the picnic blanket. It takes off over the hills, roaring with pride. It's a <kanji>dragon</kanji> now.
竜.on: It flies home for the family <sound>reu</sound>nion, and every aunt gasps.
竜.kun: It toasts a <sound>ta</sound>co for each aunt, then lands in the lake with a <sound>tsu</sound>nami.

架.meaning: A beaver wants to <part>add</part> one wonder to the forest, so it props a fallen <part>tree</part> upright, braces it with twigs and fixes crossbeams to it, a tall frame by sunset. The other animals gasp: it found a way to <kanji>erect</kanji> a tower.
架.on: From the top it can see a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the pond far below.
架.kun: It hangs a sign from the frame: 'Stay <sound>ca</sound>lm, it holds.'

粒.meaning: At a tiny parade, every <part>rice</part> kernel is ordered to <part>stand</part> to attention in single file along a chopstick, a million long. An ant general inspects them one by one through a magnifying glass, counting all the <kanji>grains</kanji>.
粒.on: Afterwards they all hop back into the bag for a <sound>reu</sound>nion.
粒.kun: Then a <sound>tsu</sound>nami of spilt soup sweeps them onto a <sound>bu</sound>ll's nose, and he sneezes.

臓.meaning: Under the <part>moon</part>, a toy maker opens his clockwork bear like a <part>storehouse</part>: inside are coiled springs, cogs, a tiny drum for a heart and a tangle of wires. He oils each one by lamplight. Even a toy has <kanji>entrails</kanji>.
臓.on: The bear's heart drum is painted with all the signs of the <sound>zo</sound>diac.
臓.kun: Inside he also finds a <sound>ha</sound>rp string, a <sound>ra</sound>men noodle, a dab of <sound>wa</sound>sabi and a <sound>ta</sound>co shell.

胸.meaning: A <part>villain</part> steals the <part>moon</part> and tries to <part>wrap</part> it in his cloak, but it glows right through. He hugs it close against his chest, where it shines like a lamp. For one night he's gentle, holding the moon to his <kanji>bosom</kanji>.
胸.on: He whispers that he'll take it to <sound>Kyo</sound>to, drawing out the start of the name like a lullaby.
胸.kun: A <sound>moo</sound>se catches him in a <sound>ne</sound>t and hangs the moon back up.

芽.meaning: In spring, an old elephant naps in the <part>grass</part> and wakes to find a tiny green shoot growing from his <part>tusk</part>, with one shy leaf. He carries it proudly for weeks, watering it with his trunk. It's his very first <kanji>bud</kanji>.
芽.on: Then a <sound>ga</sound>rlic bulb starts sprouting from his other tusk.
芽.kun: Next a <sound>me</sound>lon seed sprouts behind his ear, and he waters that too.

砕.meaning: A grumpy troll hates the <part>signpost</part> that keeps pointing tourists to his bridge, so he hurls a <part>stone</part> at it. Crack! It bursts into a hundred splinters. The tourists find him anyway, but it felt good to <kanji>smash</kanji> it.
砕.on: To calm down, he sips a jug of <sound>ci</sound>der under the bridge.
砕.kun: His friend the <sound>coo</sound>k bakes him a <sound>du</sound>ck-shaped pie to cheer him up.

潜.meaning: A spy and a fish <part>exchange</part> clothes so the spy can sneak past the castle guards. In borrowed scales he slips into the moat, sending up a few <part>water drops</part>, and holds his breath. The fish waddles off in a trench coat. The spy must <kanji>submerge</kanji>.
潜.on: The <sound>sen</sound>try on the wall waves at the fish, sure it's the spy.
潜.kun: Down in the moat he hides behind a sunken <sound>hee</sound>l and an old <sound>so</sound>fa.

粘.meaning: A <part>fortune telling</part> booth at the fair hands out <part>rice</part> balls instead of cards: squeeze one, and your future is whatever gets stuck to your fingers. One man gets a beetle, a coin and a lost earring. The future, it turns out, is <kanji>sticky</kanji>.
粘.on: He wipes his hands on the teller's tablecloth of white li<sound>nen</sound>.
粘.kun: '<sound>Ne</sound>xt!' calls the teller. '<sound>Bah</sound>,' grumbles the man, still stuck to his stool.

鼻.meaning: A giant naps in a <part>rice field</part> with a <part>goal</part> post propped on his face as glasses. When he sneezes, the blast blows the door off a <part>phone booth</part> a mile away. Farmers bring him a hanky the size of a sail for his enormous <kanji>nose</kanji>.
鼻.on: A <sound>bee</sound>tle walking up his face tickles him into one more sneeze.
鼻.kun: That sneeze sends a <sound>ha</sound>rp and a basket of <sound>na</sound>an flying over the hills.

臨.meaning: A palace <part>servant</part> walks to the end of the <part>diving board</part> with a tray of <part>goods</part> for the queen, but she's floating far off in the pool. He shades his eyes and peers across the water for her signal. All he can do is <kanji>look to</kanji> her.
臨.on: At last she raises a hand flashing a gold <sound>rin</sound>g: jump!
臨.kun: Until then he's <sound>no</sound>t moving at all, stiff as a <sound>zo</sound>mbie on the board.

紋.meaning: Granny's family has an odd tradition: once a year a <part>dancer</part> twirls inside a ball of gold <part>thread</part>, and the tangled shape left on the floor is stitched onto every coat. This year it looks like a sneezing owl. That's the new <kanji>family crest</kanji>.
紋.on: Last year's looked like a <sound>mon</sound>ster wearing three hats.

濃.meaning: Two <part>farmers</part> boil a whole orchard of berries down until only a few <part>water drops</part> are left, black and syrupy. One drop on a pancake makes a kid's eyes water. It's the most <kanji>concentrated</kanji> jam ever made.
濃.on: A garden <sound>gno</sound>me licks the spoon, and his hat turns purple.
濃.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala tries one drop and sleeps for a week.

淡.meaning: A camp cook heats a pot over a big <part>flame</part>, but every time more hikers arrive he adds more <part>water drops</part> to stretch it. By dinner the soup is barely coloured, and you can see the spoon through it. The soup is sadly <kanji>thin</kanji>.
淡.on: He serves it in a dark <sound>tun</sound>nel so nobody can see how weak it is.
淡.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' sighs a hiker, 'a spoon of <sound>wa</sound>sabi would help.'
